Harbor ferry fares rise for the winter season

The ferry company will raise its winter fares by a tenth from the first of December, the harbor office said on Tuesday, after a summer in which the crossing ran at a loss for the first time in eleven years.

The company blamed the price of fuel and the cost of repairing the north landing, which the October storms left without its outer rail.

Season tickets bought before the end of November keep the old price, and children under twelve still cross free with an adult. The harbor office will publish the new timetable beside the fares on the notice board at the south landing and in the weekly paper.

Residents who cross every day have asked the town council for a commuter fare, and the council has said it will hear them at its next meeting. The lighthouse keepers' association has asked for the same.

The council meets again in March, when the bookbinder's petition about the ledger will be read as well.

The fares ordinance

1. Who pays the winter fare

Every passenger over twelve pays the winter fare on every crossing made between the first of December and the last day of February, whatever landing the crossing starts from, unless a season ticket bought before the first of December covers the crossing, in which case the summer fare printed on the ticket applies until it ends.
